name: Ana — the ordinary case
summary: Around 70 hours over three seasons, about ten hours last year, flying roughly monthly. Can climb in a thermal but loses the core. Reads the day about half right. Tries to react in the bumps but it isn't automatic. Sensible, honest, no drama anywhere, and nobody qualified has watched her fly for a while.
why_this_persona: The most common real outcome and the one no other persona covers: Nearly ready on the total alone, with no gate and no rule. Because the engine only tags a threshold rule when the total would otherwise have reached Ready, her 'rules_expected' must be empty — which is the specific behaviour this persona pins down.

notes: Computed skills 64.1, psychological 84.7, total 74.0, no bonus. The total sits just under the Ready threshold of 75, which widened from A to low-B's 72 precisely so that an ordinary profile like hers lands in the middle band rather than scraping a Ready at the softest boundary on the ladder. See meta.design_decisions 'v1-wider-nearly-ready-band'.

'rules_expected' must be empty. She would fail critical_check_floor on thermal_turn_control (0.45) and active_piloting (0.45), and her skills score is below the Ready floor of 66 — but the engine only reports threshold rules when the total itself reached the Ready threshold, and hers did not. A scorer that reports a rule here is reporting a reason that is not the actual reason.

Sensitivity note for the owner: she is the persona most affected by the Ready threshold. At 72 (A to low-B's figure) her total would reach the Ready threshold and she would then be held at Nearly ready by two reported rules instead — 'ready_category_floor:skills' (64.1 against a floor of 66) and 'critical_check_floor:thermal_turn_control' — so the recommendation would be the same but the explanation on screen would change. Her recommendation only becomes Ready if the threshold drops to 74 or below AND the skills floor drops below 64.1 AND thermal_turn_control leaves critical_check_floor.questions, which is three deliberate loosenings rather than one.

She is also the clearest illustration that the in-air cluster carries this rubric: her hours and flight count are unremarkable but acceptable, and what actually holds her back is thermalling, reading the day and active hands.
